title: DEMOCRATIZING OPEN AND COMPLIANT LLMS FOR GLOBAL LANGUAGE ENVIRONMENTS

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluated using the BBQ (Bias Benchmark for QA) dataset to elicit implicit biases, and through qualitative red-teaming prompts assessing gender stereotypes in career advice and job screening scenarios.
Evaluated using the BBQ benchmark and through qualitative red-teaming prompts designed to test for racial stereotyping in customer service contexts and racial tropes in storytelling.
Evaluated using the BBQ benchmark and through qualitative red-teaming prompts assessing the model's reliance on ableist language or assumptions in healthcare advice scenarios.
Evaluated using the BBQ (Bias Benchmark for QA) multiple-choice dataset, which probes for implicit biases against various demographic categories, including age.

Evaluated by calculating a Tokenizer Fairness Gini Coefficient to measure the inequality of tokenization costs across different languages, and by assessing performance disparities on multilingual safety and cultural benchmarks.

Evaluated by using an 'Ideological Sensitivity Classifier' to identify controversial prompts, and applying a Constitutional AI LLM-as-a-judge approach (based on the Swiss AI Charter) to measure the model's neutrality, impartiality, and consensus-building capabilities on sensitive topics.
